subject: Order form — clarify audit access, pen-test windows, and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightspring.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightSpring Legal <legal@brightspring.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify audit access & pen-test language for Order Form

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the draft order form — legal here at BrightSpring had a few open items we need to close before procurement can route. Short list: SOC 2 attestation timing (do you have a rolling report or an annual letter we can reference?), pen-test notification window and whether you allow a third-party assessor to observe, and a bit more granularity on evidence cadence (we need to map deliverables to our procurement milestone schedule).

A few specifics from our side:
- We typically ask for a 14-day notice for penetration testing, but we can be flexible depending on staging access.
- We need confirmation that any inspection is scoped to non-production or bounded sample sets and that PII access will be redacted/obfuscated.
- For SOC2, we require a recent attestation and the ability to request the auditor contact if follow-ups are needed.

Could you confirm Redwood's standard positions and, if possible, share the pen-test checklist or SOC2 summary we can attach to the order form?

Happy to schedule a quick call if that's easier. We are trying to close legal review by next Friday (10/9).

Thanks —
Elena Morales
Sr. Contracts Manager, BrightSpring Health
elena.morales@brightspring.com
+1 617-555-0142

Attachments: none in this message
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightspring.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T12:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit access & pen-test language for Order Form

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front and then a few proposed contract-friendly carveouts so procurement can move: 

1) SOC 2: we can provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (2025) under an NDA; summary and control mapping attached for your auditors. We can also provide auditor contact details on request for follow-ups.

2) Pen test notice window: our standard is 30 days for full-scope/production-impacting tests. For non-invasive or staging-only tests we can accept 14 days. We propose language that differentiates invasive tests (root-level, live production) vs. non-invasive/staging runs.

3) Scope & sampling: we support bounded inspection and sample-sets. We do not allow uncontrolled forensic access to live production environments. Staging access can be made available via ephemeral credentials and a jumpbox/VPN; we keep session records and can provide session logs as evidence.

4) Evidence cadence: we typically surface a SOC2 summary and a pen-test checklist + remediation status. For onboarding you should expect an initial evidence packet (SOC2 summary, control mappings, pen-test checklist) and then weekly status updates during the onboarding window (4 weeks max) if there are active remediation items. After onboarding, we provide annual attestation and ad-hoc follow-ups tied to contract triggers.

Please find attached: SOC2_Report_2025.pdf (redacted for public consumption) and pen-test-checklist.xlsx (internal checklist with test categories and typical remediation timelines).

If BrightSpring wants to tighten the notice period to 14 days, we can accept that for staging/non-invasive tests but will ask for a carveout for high-risk/invasive tests that require 30 days and a change control plan. We can also add obligations for both parties to coordinate a pre-test runbook and an agreed scope doc so there are no surprises.

If that approach works, can you share the specific redlines you plan to propose on the Order Form? I copied Karthik (legal) and Monica (security ops) to confirm the carveouts and practical ops. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call — I have availability Thu 10/3 10–11 AM PT.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Assurance & Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachments:
- SOC2_Report_2025.pdf (summary, redacted)
- pen-test-checklist.xlsx (test categories + typical remediation windows)
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightspring.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightSpring Legal <legal@brightspring.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit access & pen-test language for Order Form

Olga —

Thanks for the thorough response and the attachments — reviewed with our legal team this morning. A couple of requested redlines include (attached PDF):

- Change: Notice window 14 days for pen tests; our note: please confirm staging vs. production carveout in the clause.
- Change: Right to use an independent third-party assessor to perform the inspection; we propose language that the assessor signs Redwood's NDA and follows the agreed scope.
- Change: Evidence delivery schedule — request an initial packet within 5 business days of onboarding signature and weekly remediation updates while there are open items.

We attached BrightSpring_redlines_20261002.pdf with markups. On the operational questions: yes, we prefer SAML SSO for staging access (no shared credentials). For session logs, we need a 90-day retention window for relevant audit sessions.

Could Karthik confirm whether Redwood will accept the independent assessor language and the 90-day session log retention? For the purposes of procurement timeline, we need final contract language by 10/9.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: BrightSpring_redlines_20261002.pdf
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightspring.com>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit access & pen-test language for Order Form

Elena —

Thanks for the markups and apologies for the slightly longer turnaround — reviewed with Legal and Security. High level: we are aligned on most items but need a couple of contractable clarifications to protect both parties.

1) Independent assessor: we can accept a third-party assessor provided they: (a) sign Redwood's standard NDA, (b) agree to scoped access only (no forensic access to customer PII), and (c) coordinate with Redwood's security ops to confirm test windows. We'll add explicit language requiring Redwood approval of the assessor's scope and a pre-test runbook.

2) Notice window: we can accept 14 days for non-invasive/staging tests (per Olga). For invasive tests that could affect production stability or require root-level access, we need 30 days plus a change control plan. Proposed contract language differentiates the two classes and lists examples.

3) Session logs retention: we can provide session logs for staging and jumpbox sessions and retain them for 90 days. For any production-level traces we assert standard retention limits (per internal policy) and will provide redacted extracts for audit purposes; we will capture this in the appendix.

4) Evidence cadence: we'll commit to the initial evidence packet within 5 business days of onboarding signature and weekly remediation updates while open items exist (4-week onboarding window). After onboarding, further evidence will be event-driven or annual attestation-based.

Next steps: we will draft contract language this week reflecting the differentiated notice windows, assessor NDA requirement, scope/runbook requirement, and the session-log retention appendix. Monica — please confirm the jumpbox/session log retention mechanics so I can include exact wording.

If acceptable, can Elena confirm BrightSpring's acceptance of the proposed carveout language (14d staging / 30d invasive) and independent-assessor NDA requirement and we'll incorporate the edits into the Order Form redline?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
